question: A 70-year-old man presents with sudden right-sided weakness and aphasia with last known well time 3 hours ago. CT brain shows no haemorrhage. Blood pressure is 185/100 mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step regarding thrombolysis?

answers.text: Administer IV alteplase immediately without further checks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Blood pressure must be reduced to <185/110 mmHg before alteplase can be given; administering it at 185/100 is borderline and requires controlled lowering first.

answers.text: Lower blood pressure to <185/110 mmHg, then administer IV alteplase within the 4.5-hour window

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Current guidelines require BP <185/110 mmHg before IV alteplase. This patient is within the 4.5-hour thrombolysis window and has no haemorrhage on CT.

answers.text: Withhold thrombolysis as the patient is >65 years old

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Age alone is not an absolute contraindication to thrombolysis. Elderly patients may still benefit if the clinical criteria are met.

answers.text: Start aspirin 300 mg immediately as the primary reperfusion strategy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Aspirin is not administered before thrombolysis if the patient is a candidate for alteplase — it increases bleeding risk. Aspirin is used only when thrombolysis is not given.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key rule: BP <185/110 mmHg is required before thrombolysis. Age is not an absolute contraindication. Aspirin is reserved for when thrombolysis is not given.
Correct. Control BP to <185/110 mmHg, then give IV alteplase within 4.5 hours if no contraindications exist.
